note: Source hygiene only: one rename and three dead-assignment deletions in src/builtins/http.js. It clears ZERO Lane B cells (338 -> 338). The three ADDITIONS below are the point of retaining this artifact: resolving a duplicate definition makes the walker descend into a callee body it previously early-returned from, surfacing dynamism the duplicate was masking. Net distinct ambiguity reduction is 13 - 5 = 8, not the 13 LLP 0045 §4 predicted. An additive-only or ambiguity-only gate would have recorded this as a clean 13-entry win.

Two distinct function-scoped locals were both named `oncreate`, at http.js:4015 inside ClientRequest._ensureSocketAssigned and http.js:5877 inside Agent.createSocket. Renaming the first leaves exactly one definition, so the duplicate-definition marker no longer fires. Verified distinct and non-escaping by repo-wide rg: the only references are within their own function bodies.

entries.sourceSpan: src/builtins/http.js:2707 (deleted guarded fallback; :2811 is the unconditional assignment)
entries.proof: IncomingMessage.prototype._read carried two assignments: a guarded fallback at :2707 and an unconditional one at :2811. The unconditional assignment always wins, so the fallback was dead in every profile. Deleting it leaves one definition. Verified empirically by replaying the exact statement sequence pre- and post-edit under both stream-present and stream-absent bases: identical in all combinations.

entries.sourceSpan: src/builtins/http.js:2710 (deleted guarded fallback; :2807 is the unconditional assignment)
entries.proof: Same shape as _read: dead guarded fallback superseded by an unconditional later assignment.

Direction is INVERTED relative to _read and resume, which is why LLP 0045 got it wrong twice. Here the SECOND assignment is the dead one: at :2804 `pause` is always already callable — inherited from Readable.prototype (src/builtins/stream.js:2153) when node:stream loads, or supplied by the :2713 fallback when it does not (http.js:11 wraps the require in try/catch for exactly that case) — so the guard is false in both profiles. git show 9e9418d2^ confirms the intent: the :2713 fallback block is the NEWER code (2026-03-13) and superseded the :2804 guard without removing it.

Consequence of the single ambiguity removal above: with the duplicate gone the route is no longer ambiguous. The cell does NOT leave Lane B — no-static-enforcement-terminal persists, because the surviving callee is `function() { return this; }`, a body with zero call expressions and therefore no terminal to find. This is the measured refutation of LLP 0045 §4's claim that this item's standalone yield is 1 cell; the true yield is 0, and the cell simply moved from the duplicate-definition bucket to empty-no-mechanism.
